proof_scope: Battle-owned shadow Jev advisory adapter contract: hash-bound jev.decision.v2 receipts, accepted/abstain/blocked/error/no_match distinctions, deterministic baseline fallback, private-data egress block, no retry cascade, and unchanged judge-only score authority. Separate fixture from the main battle manifest.

claims.proves: The Battle shadow adapter emits real jev.decision.v2 receipts read back from an executed Jev client, falls back to the deterministic Battle baseline on every non-accepted/invalid/unavailable result, blocks private-artifact payloads before egress, performs exactly one Jev call per proposal with the client-owned cooldown as the only backoff, and exposes no scoring, judging, adaptive-selection, spawn-approval, or authorization surface.
claims.does_not_prove: hosted Jev judgment quality against the live typesafe endpoint, latency/cost savings, active (non-shadow) proposal application, or changes to Battle's judge_receipts_only score authority outside tested binding

capability_claims.description: Every non-accepted, malformed, nonmember, private-data, disabled, or provider-failure result preserves the caller's candidate ordering verbatim and never applies the proposal.

Accepted proposals bind jev.decision.v2 receipt hashes (request/state/questions/policy), battle/run/round identity, task and candidate hashes, a deterministic Battle-side catalog_hash over the exact normalized candidate packet sent to Jev, and per-candidate source identity.
Exactly one Jev transport call per proposal; provider 429 sets a client-owned cooldown whose second abstain makes no additional transport call.
The adapter exposes no score, judge, adaptive-selection, spawn-approval, or target-authorization functions and Battle scoring still derives from judge receipts.

cases.name: shadow-adapter-fail-closed-contract
command: cd .. && PYTHONPATH=$PWD/../jev/src uv run --project . python -m pytest tests/test_jev_shadow.py -q
